raw_response:
I've been farming these 50 mu for 25 years now — started when I was 22, taking over from my father. Back then it was all cotton. Six years ago I put 20 mu into stevia after Old Wang from the east end of the village showed me his numbers. The stevia buyer comes right to the county now, so I don't have to haul it to Xingtai myself. The other 30 mu I keep in cotton — the ginning station is only 8 li down the road, and I know that crop like the back of my hand.

My wife and I do the main management, and my son is 19. He helps between his construction jobs in Handan, but I can't rely on him full-time. With 50 mu and only two steady hands, I hire workers for the busy spells — transplanting, cutting, and especially picking. Hired labor is 160 yuan per day now, up from 120 three years ago. It stings, but there's no other way. I also rent a rotary tiller and a planter from the machinery cooperative. Doing it all by hand on this size? Impossible.

For the **cotton** on 30 mu, I plant mid-April with an improved variety from the county seed station. I learned my lesson about cheap seed twelve years ago — half-empty bolls and I lost nearly 4,000 yuan that year. Never again. I spread compound fertilizer before planting, about 50 kg per mu worked into the soil, and then topdress with urea at flowering — about 15 kg per mu. The extension guy says 15 kg N per mu is the target, but my south field is a bit sandy and leaches, so I push it to around 16-17 kg N total. I irrigate three times: once right after planting to get emergence, once at flowering in July, and once at boll filling in August. The water bill keeps going up, but dry cotton drops its bolls, and that's a disaster I can't afford. For chemicals, I spray herbicide once early, and I watch for bollworm like a hawk. I'll do a preventive insecticide spray at flowering, and if I see damage in August I'll hit it again. I expect about 300 kg per mu of seed cotton if the weather cooperates.

For the **stevia** on 20 mu, I transplant seedlings in late April that I buy from a nursery in Xingtai. They're not cheap — about 100 yuan per mu — but starting stevia from seed myself takes too long and the germination is spotty. Stevia leaves need rich soil, so I put down plenty of base fertilizer: about 60 kg of compound fertilizer per mu. Then I topdress twice — about 15 kg urea per mu after the first cut in late July, and again in mid-August — because the plants need nitrogen to push out new leaves for the second harvest. I irrigate four times total; stevia doesn't like dry spells if you want sweet leaves. I harvest twice: first cut in late July, second in mid-September. After cutting, I hire 4-5 workers to help strip leaves and I dry them in the shed I built three years ago. I figure on about 200 kg of dried leaves per mu. The price has been 13-15 yuan per kg the last couple years, which beats cotton on a per-mu basis, but the input costs are higher and the market is narrower.

My total input costs — seed, fertilizer, pesticide, water — will run about 22,000 yuan this year. Hired labor will be another big chunk, maybe 15,000 yuan or more depending on how many days I need. It's a lot of money going out before anything comes in. I'm a little worried about the electricity rates for pumping — they raised them again last winter — and if bollworm hits hard or stevia gets leaf spot, I could lose 15-20%. But that's farming. You spread your risk, you watch your costs, and you do what you know works. I've seen good years and bad years, and I'm still here.
